item.text: {"question_id":"3B.7","answer":"During 2023, the administration supported a substantial but uneven protection infrastructure. Measures included national and subnational gender-violence reforms, training for 8,400 public servants, strengthened migrant-child protection routes, a fourfold increase in COMAR capacity since 2018, digital asylum case management, anti-trafficking routes, displacement-response coordination, and services for children, pregnant women, migrants, refugees, and other vulnerable groups (BATCH-0015-E016; BATCH-0015-E017; BATCH-0015-E012; BATCH-0015-E004). Some responses produced concrete reach: authorities in Michoacán responded to mass displacement within 48 hours with UN support, and UN agencies and partners delivered thousands of shelter, education, nutrition, and protection interventions. These outputs were frequently joint or externally supported, so they demonstrate institutional activity and partial protection rather than presidentially attributable nationwide effectiveness (BATCH-0015-E016; BATCH-0015-E012). Contrary evidence shows that protection was not equitable or reliably enforced. The 2023 asylum surge saturated an under-resourced system; shelters reached more than 300% of optimal capacity in some areas and many people remained in improvised camps (BATCH-0015-E017; BATCH-0015-E012). CNDH found that the migrant-child protection route had unresolved entry and best-interests problems, inconsistent protocols, incomplete records, inadequate staffing and budgets, large gaps between people referred and served, and no uniform guarantee of effective protection across states (BATCH-0015-E007). Amnesty documented continuing femicides, approximately eleven women killed daily in official data, inadequate investigations, impunity, lost evidence, and family revictimization despite gender-violence alerts (BATCH-0051-E009). A migrant-detention fire killed at least 40 people after detainees were reportedly left behind locked doors, while authorities remained unable to adequately protect migrants’ life and security (BATCH-0004-E006). UN findings also recorded widespread arbitrary detention, detention of migrant children contrary to legal restrictions, discrimination and violence affecting Indigenous people, negligible psychosocial-disability treatment, and reprisals involving advocates for LGBTI+, Indigenous, and Afro-Mexican communities (BATCH-0049-E011). The evidence therefore supports partial, mixed protection with recurring and sometimes severe failures in implementation, access, and remedy. It does not establish that every local or subnational failure was personally directed by the president; the strongest presidential attribution concerns federal migration, security, and institutional policy, while many service and enforcement outcomes remain shared across federal, state, municipal, UN, and civil-society actors.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E004","BATCH-0015-E012","BATCH-0015-E016","BATCH-0015-E017"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0004-E006","BATCH-0004-E013","BATCH-0015-E007","BATCH-0049-E011","BATCH-0051-E009","BATCH-0045-E002"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The evidence is strongest for women, migrant children, refugees, Indigenous people, persons with disabilities, LGBTI+ people, journalists, and defenders; coverage of all minorities and vulnerable groups is incomplete.","Many positive measures are laws, capacity inputs, partner-supported programs, or reported reach rather than independently demonstrated nationwide outcomes.","Several adverse findings concern institutions across federal, state, and municipal levels and do not establish personal presidential responsibility for each incident.","The supplied evidence does not provide a complete national measure of equitable access across regions or a full counterfactual for displacement and intergroup violence."],"corrections_made":["Separated formal reforms and program capacity from demonstrated implementation and outcomes.","Added the strong 2023 COMAR expansion and asylum-system saturation, shelter overload, and displacement-response evidence.","Replaced the unsupported general claim of disability and Indigenous exclusion with specifically supported evidence on Indigenous discrimination, psychosocial-disability neglect, and minority-rights reprisals.","Retained explicit limits on presidential attribution, subnational responsibility, external support, and nationwide effectiveness."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Reopen if additional supplied evidence materially documents nationwide funding, enforcement orders, equitable regional access, or direct presidential responsibility for the cited protection failures.","Reopen if evidence distinguishes the administration’s own migration and security decisions from inherited or subnational institutional weaknesses more precisely."]}
